name: Enjin CryptoItems ERC-1538 registry adapter initialize manager takeover
summary: Two Enjin ERC-1538 adapter registries route the adapter template's initialize(uint256) through their own fallback, so it runs in registry storage and writes the caller into the pending-manager slot. The attacker took both registries, routed adapter selectors to its own code, then pulled others' items through new adapters without approval and melted them for ENJ.
notes: Each registry's reset is the FunctionUpdate that routed initialize(uint256) to its adapter template, the only such route before the exploit; registry A's came two blocks after B's and sets the age. The later pending-manager setting was overwritten by the exploit and was not needed.

Campaign: every later attacker transaction in which the ENJ reserve paid out; no other party drained the reserve afterwards. Loss counts the reserve's ENJ only, including amounts melt calls paid to other recipients; stolen items that were not melted are not valued.
CryptoItems' melt route changed in 2021, but melting works as designed and carries no defect, so CryptoItems is not a target.
